task_and_failure: The two required whole-suite jobs run the whole unittest suite (9,943 ids in 234 test files at base 9b0b8d6d, by this record's inventory gate) in one process: validate (validate.yml, ubuntu-24.04, 4 vCPUs, the image's system CPython 3.12) took 1,727 to 1,828 s per job and validate-macos (adoption-bootstrap.yml, macos-15, 3 cores, actions/setup-python 3.13) a median 1,842 s for its full-suite step in plan W1's samples of 2026-10-02/03 (not re-measured here). The first trial (unittest-parallel 1.8.6, draft pull request 646, run 37109532421) failed its preregistered rule on Linux because that runner pickles live TestCase instances (an IsolatedAsyncioTestCase holds a contextvars.Context; four dynamically built classes are not importable by name), and macOS was never measured. This second trial asks, per OS and by a rule fixed here before any hosted run, whether the same suite run as N concurrent single-process shards inside one job, with GitHub's native parallel steps (each shard python3 -m unittest -v <its test files>), reproduces the serial outcomes exactly and is fast enough to adopt in a later, separately reviewed pull request. Status planned: nothing has run on a GitHub-hosted runner for this record, and nothing is adopted.

license_and_compatibility: No package is added: the shards are GitHub-native parallel steps running the interpreter each production job already uses, and every script of this directory is Python standard library only. Compatibility: each shard is python3 -m unittest -v <test files>, which loads the named modules with the stock loader (load_tests receives the pattern None), so nothing is pickled and dynamically built classes load as they do in production; the inventory gate requires that loading every test file by name gives exactly the ids discovery gives. Shards built from files keep wrapper modules whole. Each job keeps its name, so the required contexts would not change. Module fixtures run once per module as in the serial run, and test files that share a shard share a process; files in different shards no longer share one.

baseline_and_candidate.baseline: Arm S on each runner: python3 -m unittest -v from the checkout root in one step, with the suite environment of the production job (Linux: the four suite-environment steps of validate.yml; macOS: actions/setup-python 3.13 plus the two npm pins, because the trial's jobs are not recorded gaps of the runtime tripwires). That is validate-macos's command and validate's command plus -v for per-test lines.
baseline_and_candidate.candidate: Sharded arms in one parallel group of shard steps, each python3 -m unittest -v <its test files>, the lists built at run time by make_shards.py from the head: on ubuntu-24.04 G4 (4 shards over every test file) and G4T (4 shards without tests.test_secret_path_guard, then that module alone in a serial tail step); on macos-15 G3 and G3T, the same with 3 shards.

predeclared_metrics.quality_rule: Fixed before any hosted run. CORPUS: the whole suite at the draft pull request's head SHA on actual GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 and macos-15 runners, one workflow per OS (suite-shards-trial-linux.yml, suite-shards-trial-macos.yml), each triggered only by the pull request's opened and reopened events with a paths filter on its own file. Every job checks out and asserts the head. INVENTORY GATE: each workflow's inventory job (ubuntu-24.04; the system python3 3.12 for Linux, actions/setup-python 3.13 for macOS) runs inventory.py, which fails the job, so that no arm runs, unless (a) loading every tests/test_*.py by name gives exactly the discovery ids, (b) no id is loaded twice, (c) nothing fails to import, and (d) every test file is in exactly one shard list or the tail of each arm, as built by make_shards.py from the frozen weights. ARMS: S, python3 -m unittest -v in one step; G4/G3, one parallel group of 4/3 shard steps, each python3 -m unittest -v <its list>; G4T/G3T, the same without tests.test_secret_path_guard plus a serial tail step that runs that module alone. Each shard step records its exit status and exits with it; its hang guard is timeout-minutes 25 on Linux and 40 on macOS. Three repeats per arm (fail-fast false); Linux at most 2 serial and 2 sharded jobs at once, macOS 1 and 1. The selection metric step_seconds is the test phase from a start step to a stop step (if: always()): the S step, or the group plus the tail, measured with time.monotonic_ns() in two processes, with the wall-clock difference kept beside it. ORACLE: compare.py with its README rules, as frozen here, parsing every log with logparse.py (the first trial's parser, copied unchanged). An S run is eligible when its log has a complete summary and no parse anomaly, its exit status agrees with its status line (zero versus non-zero), its executed ids plus the ids behind a failed or skipped setUpClass or setUpModule are exactly the inventory with each id once, its command is exactly python3 -m unittest -v, git-status.txt (git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all after the run) exists and is empty, run_attempt is 1, checkout_sha is the head, its job was not cancelled, and step_ns and wall_ns are positive and agree within max(5 s, 1 %); the eligible S runs must share one python version. A G or GT run is eligible when every shard log and the tail meet the same log rules, every command is exactly python3 -m unittest -v followed by its list, the run's lists equal the inventory artifact's, each log's executed ids are exactly its modules' ids, the union over all logs is exactly the inventory with each id once (a module in two shards or an id that never started is ineligible), the multiset of (kind, key, outcome) records equals the first eligible S run's outside the flaky ids, every step's probe shows the job's python version and it equals S's, and the checkout, attempt, head, job status and timing rules hold. Flaky ids are ids whose records differ among the eligible S runs; they are listed in result.json and excluded from the comparison. No id is exempt in advance. The inventory artifact must record a passed gate and its lists must equal make_shards.py's lists for its test files and the frozen weights, or the OS gets no verdict. CONTROLS, per OS: one job runs the shard step body in one parallel group on four control modules copied alone into an empty directory: test_ctl_pass (exit 0, Ran 2, OK), test_ctl_fail (FAILED (failures=1), a non-zero exit), test_ctl_crash (os._exit(3): exit 3, no summary) and test_ctl_hang (300 s sleep under timeout-minutes 1: stopped, so no exit status and no summary). The controls pass only when the control job's result is failure, every shard behaved as listed with the exact command, every background step ran the foreground step's python version and saw SUITE_SHARDS_ENV_PROBE, exported through GITHUB_ENV by an earlier step, the control run's checkout is clean, its run_attempt is 1 and its head is the pull request head; a controls-check job (needs controls, if always) asserts this and the compare job requires it. Whether background steps start with SIGINT or SIGQUIT ignored is recorded in every probe and reported, not judged; any effect on the suite shows as a record mismatch. DECISION RULE, per OS: an arm is eligible when it has three runs, every run is eligible, and (for G and GT) the OS controls passed. S must be eligible, or the OS gets no verdict. No eligible sharded arm gives reject. Otherwise take the eligible sharded arm with the smaller median step_seconds (a tie goes to the arm without a tail) and adopt it only if its median is at most 3/5 of the S median and its slowest run at most 3/4 of the fastest S run, both compared as exact fractions of nanoseconds with no rounding before the comparison; otherwise reject, with no fall-through to the other arm. A cancelled or skipped job, a missing run directory, a job status cancelled or a missing control run makes the OS incomplete, which is recorded as such and is never a rule outcome; a failed inventory gate or an unusable inventory artifact gives no verdict. result.json and summary.md list every preregistered OS; each workflow measures its own, and the other is listed as no verdict with the reason no run directory. The ubuntu-24.04 verdict decides a Linux adoption pull request and the macos-15 verdict a macOS one, independently. RE-RUNS: the trial is repeated only by closing and reopening the draft pull request; a job re-run voids the arm-run it touches (run_attempt must be 1), every upload sets overwrite false, and every attempt is reported.
predeclared_metrics.usage_rule: No usage claim. The hosted runs execute deterministic commands and no model; their usage fields are observed zeros for deterministic execution, never a savings claim. The model usage of the sessions that planned and built this trial is not recorded here and stays unknown; it is neither estimated nor counted as zero.

runtime_and_platform.isolation: A draft pull request that is never merged. The workflows trigger only on that pull request's opened and reopened events with a paths filter on their own files, run with contents: read, persist-credentials false and no secrets, and change no other workflow, required check or ruleset. Each job runs on a fresh hosted VM. Run directories, the control suite and the inventory live under RUNNER_TEMP, outside the checkout, and the checkout must be clean after every run. Artifacts are kept 30 days.

commands: One parallel group of N shard steps (N = 4 on ubuntu-24.04, 3 on macos-15), each python3 -m unittest -v <the test files of its list>, then for G4T and G3T the serial tail python3 -m unittest -v tests.test_secret_path_guard

Controls: the shard step body in one parallel group on test_ctl_pass, test_ctl_fail, test_ctl_crash and test_ctl_hang (timeout-minutes 5, 5, 5 and 1), then python3 blueprints/convergence-practice/suite-shards-trial-20261003/compare.py controls --dir <results>/<os>-controls --os <os> --job-result <needs.controls.result> --expected-sha <head>

Oracle: python3 -m unittest discover -s blueprints/convergence-practice/suite-shards-trial-20261003 -p test_*.py -v; then python3 blueprints/convergence-practice/suite-shards-trial-20261003/compare.py verdict --results <results> --inventory <inventory> --expected-sha <head> --os <os> --needs needs.json --out result.json --summary-md summary.md --checkout-status checkout-status.json
limitations: Planned only. No GitHub-hosted run exists for this record. The evidence so far is local integration evidence (the coordinator's whole-suite preflight, this unit's inventory gate at the base, the oracle's dry run on the preflight's real logs, the oracle's own tests) and synthetic fixtures (real local runs of a fixture suite and of the controls). None of it is upstream acceptance.

The preflight ran on another machine (48 cores, against 4 vCPUs and 3 cores on the hosted runners), another CPython patch release (3.13.16, against the Linux runner's 3.12) and an earlier base (d2777ee7, 233 test files, against 234 at the trial base). Its shard lists differ from the trial's in how the small files are partitioned, and the trial adds one file, so its equality evidence covers different process groupings than the hosted runs will use.

n = 3 runs per arm. Hosted wall-clock time varies with neighbours and image updates (the first trial's three serial Linux runs took 1,186 to 1,688 s on one image); three repeats bound this loosely. Job seconds from the jobs API are reported beside step_seconds and are not used by the rule.
Hosted macOS has never run this suite in shards, and the first trial never ran on macOS at all.

Whether a hosted runner starts background steps with SIGINT or SIGQUIT ignored, whether earlier GITHUB_ENV exports and actions/setup-python's PATH reach background steps, and whether timeout-minutes stops a background step are not documented on the pages read. The controls and every shard's probe measure them; locally, ignored dispositions skipped a SIGQUIT subtest, which the record comparison would count as a mismatch.

zizmor 1.30.1 warns that its support for parallel steps is experimental (its docs/usage.md at v1.30.1, 'Parallel steps'), so its audit coverage inside the groups is not established; the shard steps are plain run steps with no expression in their scripts. actionlint 1.17.0 parses the groups and runs shellcheck on their scripts.

The macOS inventory is built on ubuntu-24.04 with the arms' Python line from the same actions/setup-python pin, so that a stalled macOS queue cannot hold it. A platform-dependent id would make every macOS S run ineligible (its executed ids must equal the inventory), which gives no verdict, not a wrong one.

The trial environment is not production's. Every arm adds -v, which Linux production lacks. The macOS arms install the two npm pins that validate-macos (a recorded gap of the runtime tripwires) does not, so those tests run in the trial and skip in production; the macOS arms also skip validate-macos's validators and bootstrap and recording smoke.

Skip reasons are not compared (the parser reads skipped '<reason>' as skipped), and side effects that leave outcomes unchanged are invisible to the oracle. Test files that share a shard share a process; files in different shards do not, so any coupling between files shows only through outcomes.

tests.test_secret_path_guard.K4GuardTests.test_k4_timing is timing-bound (30 to 60 s serially) and failed under class-level parallel load in the first trial; the T arms keep its module out of the parallel group, the G arms do not. A mismatch on it counts under the rule like any other; only the flaky-id rule excludes an id.
A file newer than the weights takes the mean weight: at the base, tests.test_catalog_freshness_runtime (5,450 ms assumed, 0.23 s locally), so its shard is predicted about 5 s heavier than it is.

Run directories and artifacts expire (artifacts after 30 days, run records under the repository's 90-day retention), so the observed record keeps sanitized durable receipts in the repository rather than run links alone. Hosted logs carry runner paths in tracebacks; scripts/validate.py rejects home paths, so receipts must be sanitized first.

The workflows, the generator, the weights, the inventory gate, the recorder, the parser, the oracle, its tests, the fixture tool, the fixture index, the controls and README.md are frozen here by hash; any later edit to one of them must refreeze this record in the same commit. The fixture logs are frozen through fixtures/index.json, which test_compare.py checks. The checker verifies declared consistency and artifact hashes, not truth or that this freeze preceded execution; the commit history and the hosted run timestamps show the order.

decision_and_scope.scope: The draft pull request that holds this record and its two trial workflows, never merged: the preregistered comparison of sharded arms (GitHub parallel steps, one unittest process per shard) against the serial whole-suite command on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 and macos-15 runners at its head. Nothing is adopted under this planned record; validate and validate-macos keep their serial commands unless an observed record meets the rule for that OS and a separate adoption pull request lands through the required checks.

rollback: Close the draft pull request. It is never merged, so main, the required checks, the rulesets and both production workflows stay unchanged; its artifacts expire after 30 days. If an adoption pull request lands later, reverting it restores the serial command (python3 -m unittest in validate, python3 -m unittest -v in validate-macos).
next_decision_changing_test: Push the branch once and open the draft pull request (lane:foundation, with the template's SOTA sources section filled in); opening it starts both trial workflows. Never push to the branch again (pushes do not re-run the trial, by design) and never re-run a job; to repeat the trial, close and reopen the pull request, and report every run and attempt. When a workflow's compare job ends, download its compare artifact (result.json, summary.md, checkout-status.json) and the inventory, controls and arm artifacts, and write the observed record in a separate records pull request: an outcome decision record, a receipt and sanitized artifacts (with a byte copy of this preregistration), plus one native_cli_execution observation per timed arm-run (task whole-suite-<os>; role arm-s, arm-g4, arm-g4t, arm-g3 or arm-g3t; condition baseline for S and candidate otherwise; attempt the repeat; command_index 0 for S and 1 otherwise; one scope text per OS). A run's status is passed only when it is eligible under the rule; each observation keeps its hashed sanitized artifacts and the jobs API's step and job seconds. Adopt within an OS's scope only if that OS's verdict is adopt, through a separately reviewed adoption pull request that builds the shard lists at run time inside the production job, updates tests/test_workflow_hardening.py for sharded whole-suite jobs and adds a shard-coverage guard test. Otherwise record reject, no verdict or incomplete as a failed or partial attempt and keep the serial command. To triage first, read the inventory job's report, then each control shard's probe (background SIGINT and SIGQUIT dispositions, SUITE_SHARDS_ENV_PROBE, python version), then the first ineligible run's reasons in result.json.
